issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a static method named acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int), and the template commented example in Main calls acceptSupplyDelivery(...). The provided solution, however, implements a static method named receiveDelivery(String, int, int) instead. This name mismatch (acceptSupplyDelivery vs. receiveDelivery) is a structural inconsistency that will confuse students about which method to implement and may cause tests or example code to fail to compile/run if they expect the name from the problem statement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across artifacts. Either rename the solution's receiveDelivery(...) method to acceptSupplyDelivery(...), and provide a matching static method in the SealSaloon class, or update the problem statement and template Main examples to use receiveDelivery(...). Ensure tests and documentation reference the same method name.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML and task text) and the template's example usage refer to a static method named acceptSupplyDelivery(...) for adding delivered ingredients to the shared stock, but the solution implementation names this method receiveDelivery(...). This inconsistent method name for the same conceptual operation (accepting a supply delivery and updating stock) can confuse students mapping the requirements and example code to the expected implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent method name for the operation across artifacts. Rename the solution's receiveDelivery(...) method to acceptSupplyDelivery(...) (keeping the same parameters and static behavior), or alternatively update the problem statement and template examples to use receiveDelivery(...). Prefer changing the solution to acceptSupplyDelivery to match the problem and template.
